primitives.name: Time-to-Arrival Quantile
primitives.verbatim_quote: We study time-to-arrival (TTA) in sports: the shortest plausible time a player needs to reach an arbitrary location on the pitch given their current kinematic state, estimated as the lower envelope of observed locomotion times.
primitives.assumptions: Player motion constrained by kinematic limits; target location fixed; observed locomotion times follow a distribution with lower quantile defining feasibility.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player kinematics exceed modeled acceleration or deceleration bounds.

layer2.mapping: TTA quantile serves as a derived kernel for spatial reachability in GSI's probabilistic motion model.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute error between predicted and actual TTA from tracking data.

primitives.name: Conditional Quantile Regression
primitives.verbatim_quote: Rather than modeling space ownership through position density estimation or closed-form physics-based models, we cast TTA as a conditional quantile regression problem, estimating the lower quantile of locomotion time so the model learns a player's lower-envelope arrival time.
primitives.assumptions: Conditional distribution of TTA is skewed; lower quantile captures feasible motion paths.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When kinematic state does not align with training data distribution.

layer2.mapping: Quantile regression is isomorphic to GSI’s belief propagation over motion feasibility.
layer2.telemetry: Pinball loss at \tau = 0.05 for TTA prediction accuracy.

primitives.name: Multilayer Perceptron for TTA
primitives.verbatim_quote: We train the model on optical tracking data from all 64 matches of the PFF FC FIFA World Cup 2022 dataset, and evaluate a lightweight multilayer perceptron against six player-motion models from the literature, re-expressed as TTA predictors, and a learned reachablehull baseline.
primitives.assumptions: Data-driven model generalizes across sports; MLP approximates complex non-linear TTA mapping.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When tracking data lacks diversity or contains sensor noise.

layer2.mapping: MLP-derived TTA estimates serve as kernel for GSE's motion lattice transition probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of TTA predictions vs. physics-based baselines on cross-sport datasets.

The core insight is that time-to-arrival (TTA) in sports is not a deterministic function but a stochastic process bounded by human locomotive capability. By framing TTA as a conditional quantile regression, the model learns the lower envelope of possible arrival times—i.e., the fastest plausible path a player can take to a target. This approach avoids the pitfalls of mean-based prediction, which can be skewed by outliers or inefficient motion. The use of a multilayer perceptron allows for flexible, data-driven modeling of complex kinematic behavior without assuming a fixed physical model. The empirical validation across sports datasets confirms robustness of this formulation. In GSI, this translates to probabilistic spatial control surfaces where reachability is expressed as a quantile of motion feasibility. In GSE, it enables tactical reasoning by modeling player motion as a sequence of state transitions governed by TTA constraints.
